meta.scenario: house relative major-to-minor move (nB→nA) — mood shift from bright to dark, high EQ management for competing hi-hat patterns, from_bar skips T2 near-silent lead-in
meta.source: Larry Heard - Live at Smartbar Chicago 2019

transition_arc: 2B (D major) → 2A (B minor) is the relative major-to-minor move — the safest possible mood shift on the Camelot wheel. Both keys share all 7 diatonic notes; there is zero harmonic clash. The audience hears the transition as an emotional shift from bright/uplifting (major) to introspective/darker (minor) without a dissonant moment. T2 has a 12-bar near-silent lead-in (RMS < 0.05) before the groove starts at bar 12 — from_bar is set to 12 to skip it. T1's outro has busy 16th-note hi-hats that would clash with T2's slower hat pattern during overlap. eq(T1, high=0.7) is used during the overlap to duck T1's hats without killing the top-end entirely.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 0: bright major-key house groove, piano chords+bass+busy hats, RMS 0.55
T1 bar 64: 8 bars before T2 fade_in at bar 72. Outro starting, busy 16th-note hi-hats active, drums=0.42, rms=0.38
annotated_actions.why: Bass pre-cut (low=0.0) 8 bars before T2 enters — standard. high=0.7 is applied here simultaneously because T1's 16th-note hi-hat pattern is dense and will clash with T2's slower groove hat pattern during the overlap. Duck T1's highs to 0.7 (≈−3 dB at 8 kHz shelf) to reduce hi-hat density. Unlike the low-end, high EQ can be adjusted before T2 arrives because a slight dulling of T1's hats is not audible as a problem — it sounds like a natural filter move.
Kill T2 bass at fade start — prevents dual basslines during blend. EQ is persistent; will be restored at bass_swap point.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 12: first non-silent bar — kick present, darker minor-key pads beginning, drums=0.30, harmonic=0.18
annotated_actions.why: from_bar=12 — T2 has 12 bars of near-silence (RMS < 0.05) before its groove starts. Starting the fade_in from bar 0 would waste 12 of the 16 fade bars on silence, leaving only 4 audible bars of blend. from_bar=12 means the full 16-bar window is used for audible T2 material. other:0.7 — relative major-to-minor move shares all 7 notes, zero harmonic clash; pads can be introduced at full warmth. drums:0.7 (not 0.8) — T1's hats are already ducked via eq(high=0.7), so combined hat density is manageable; no need to over-reduce T2's drums. stems={drums:0.8, bass:0.0, other:0.6} — T2 enters with 80% drums, no bass (held for bass_swap), 60% atmosphere.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 80: midpoint of fade, drums=0.22, harmonic=0.18, rms=0.22
annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 20 (from_bar=12, 8 bars elapsed): bass entering, minor-key groove establishing
annotated_actions.why: Standard midpoint (72 + 8 = 80). T1 bass cut since bar 64. The swap releases T2's minor-key bassline. At the midpoint, T1's major-key harmonic material is at 50% gain and T2's minor-key harmonic is at 50% — the relative key relationship means these coexist without dissonance. The audience may subconsciously notice the mood darkening.
Restore T2 bass at bass_swap point — T1 bass is now HPF-cut, T2 bass can come in.
Simultaneous with T2 fade_in. 16-bar fade_out. T1's bright major-key sound fades as T2's darker minor-key character rises.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 28: full minor-key house groove, bass+kick+darker pads, RMS 0.52
annotated_actions.why: T2 full groove fires. Mood shift from major to minor complete. from_bar = fade_in.from_bar(12) + fade_in.duration_bars(16) = 28. The bright 2B energy has dissolved; 2A's introspective quality is now the dominant character of the mix.
